comment: The register of which repos are frozen and why. Kept here, in MAM-basics, rather than as a marker file inside each frozen repo: writing such a marker would itself change the repo and destroy the very last-changed date the freeze exists to preserve. Deliberately separate from in/vendoring_policy.json, whose per-repo 'ignore' flag means 'do not scan this repo for vendoring' -- a different question from 'do not touch this repo at all'. The lists are not the same one: CCAR-Psalms is frozen here and is not ignored there, so neither may be derived from the other.
location_comment: Ben's decision, 2026-08-31: C:\Users\BenDe\FrozenRepos is NOT part of the expected machine layout, and no machine is to be made to have one. It was a transitional hedge -- an almost-trash staging area created on 2026-08-07, when moving the six frozen clones out of GitRepos felt safer than deleting them, and dropping them from all-repos.code-workspace took that file from 30 folders to 24 -- and the hedge is spent, because all six remotes are ARCHIVED on GitHub and so are read-only and durable. The archived remote is the copy of record; a clone was only ever a second copy of it. A machine with no FrozenRepos directory is conforming, not broken, so do not restore one and do not read its absence as a defect. WHAT ENFORCES THE FREEZE IS ABSENCE FROM A WORKSPACE FILE, NOT LOCATION: every sweep in py/main_repo_util.py iterates the repos a workspace file lists and resolves them under --repos-root, so a repo no workspace file lists cannot be reached by any action -- not just --run-black, which was the only action ever consulting this list (open issue #211). This file therefore no longer skips anything at run time, and that is not a defect either: the register's job is to record WHICH repos are frozen and WHY, which all-repos.code-workspace's silence cannot do. Two consequences of the freeze being structural. (1) A frozen repo is not swept for leftover agent worktrees either, which is fine while nothing runs sessions in a frozen clone, and is the thing to revisit if that ever changes. (2) To thaw a repo: un-archive it on GitHub, since an archived remote refuses a push with 403, then clone it back into GitRepos, re-add it to all-repos.code-workspace, and delete its entry here. HOW THE HEDGE WAS FOUND TO BE SPENT, recorded so that nobody re-diagnoses the missing directory. A sync on 2026-08-31 rebuilt this machine and did not restore FrozenRepos; nothing broke, and a full session's work noticed nothing missing. That sync restored every non-archived repo Ben owns and not one archived repo -- the six repos listed below being both the only archived ones and the only absent ones -- so the sync cannot produce FrozenRepos on any machine. Restoring the directory would be a manual act, repeated per machine, that nothing checks and nothing reminds anyone about. That is why the arrangement is retired: not because the six clones were unwanted, but because it was a fixture no mechanism maintained.

repo_visibility.comment: Which repos are public and which are private, so a maintenance sweep can keep the two apart. Declared here rather than queried from GitHub because the sweeps must work offline. Ben's decision, 2026-08-27: a repo's NAME is not itself private, so naming the private repos in this public file is fine -- what must not cross is their CONTENT, meaning paths inside them, file names of theirs, and findings about them. py/repo_util/report_destination.py is what enforces that, refusing to write a report covering a private repo into a public repo's tracked tree; py/tests/test_repo_visibility_declared.py is what keeps this map complete, failing if all-repos.code-workspace lists a folder no entry here classifies. Verified 2026-08-27 against `gh repo view bdenckla/<name> --json visibility` for the 18 first-class repos. THE SECOND HALF OF THAT VERIFICATION IS GONE, and the reason it existed is worth keeping: a nineteenth entry, Gist-ArtScroll, could not be checked that way at all, `gh repo view` being unable to resolve a gist, so it was verified with `gh api gists/f04699f2a9c4eccd3220751fdb233722 --jq .public` instead -- which is the second reason this map is declared rather than queried, and it stands for whatever gist next joins a workspace file. That entry left on 2026-08-31, when the gist's content was evacuated into MAM-basics as py/author_misc/review_of_artscroll_transliterated_linear_siddur.py and the gist dropped out of all-repos.code-workspace; the map classifies workspace folders, so a gist in no workspace file needs no entry. Its clone URL is in gitrepos_setup_rule's gists key.

gitrepos_setup_rule.comment: The complete definition of which repos belong under C:\Users\BenDe\GitRepos, so that 'set up GitRepos' on a new machine and 'sync GitRepos' on an existing one are the same reproducible question. Ben's decision, 2026-08-31: ALL-REPOS.CODE-WORKSPACE IS THE ROSTER, and only the repos it lists are to be cloned. This REPLACED a first attempt the same day, which started from `gh repo list bdenckla` and subtracted exclusion lists. Ben rejected that as too broad, and he was right for a reason worth keeping: an enumeration-minus-exclusions rule is a PROXY, and a proxy is exactly what caused the failure this key exists to prevent. The 2026-08-31 sync implemented 'on GitHub but not in GitRepos' for an instruction that had asked for repos added since Ben last used the machine, and so dragged the discontinued trope back onto the disk, because under a set difference a deliberately removed repo and a newly added one look identical. An inclusion list cannot make that mistake: a repo nobody listed is simply never cloned, and stays absent without anyone having to record why it is absent.
clauses: 1. THE ROSTER IS all-repos.code-workspace's `folders` array, and nothing else. Each path there is relative to MAM-basics: '.' is MAM-basics itself, '../X' is the sibling clone X. On 2026-08-31 that was 19 folders, having been 20 earlier the same day: Gist-ArtScroll left when its content was evacuated into MAM-basics as py/author_misc/review_of_artscroll_transliterated_linear_siddur.py, rendered to MAM-with-doc/gh-pages/misc/, and the gist itself cut down to a stub pointing at that page.
2. BOOTSTRAP by cloning MAM-basics first, since the roster lives inside it: git clone https://github.com/bdenckla/MAM-basics.git

3. CLONE each remaining folder by name. py/repo_util/repo_selection.py's _how_to_obtain() already performs exactly this mapping and is the implementation of record: https://github.com/bdenckla/<name>.git for an ordinary repo, and for a folder in its _NON_REPO_WORKSPACE_FOLDERS map the URL recorded there instead, because such a folder's clone URL is not derivable from its name. THAT MAP IS EMPTY as of 2026-08-31, Gist-ArtScroll having been its only entry, so today every folder in the roster takes the guessed URL. The map is kept, empty, because it is the one place a non-guessable folder can be declared, and the roster gaining one is a single line rather than a restored mechanism.

4. CLONE NOTHING ELSE. There is no exclusion list to consult and no GitHub enumeration to filter: whatever is not in the roster is not cloned, archived or not, fork or not, gist or not. The frozen_repos are not cloned (Ben's decision, 2026-08-31) and neither is anything in repos_to_keep_absent, but neither key is READ to reach that result -- omission alone does the work, which is what makes this rule proxy-free.

5. EXTRA CLONES ARE NOT PART OF THE TARGET STATE. On 2026-08-31 this machine held 27 clones while the roster listed 20 (19 after Gist-ArtScroll left it later that day). The extras are residue of earlier work and of repos Ben deliberately wants nowhere -- they are not evidence the roster is incomplete, and a fresh machine gets the roster and nothing more.

6. NON-REPO DIRECTORIES DO NOT BELONG UNDER GitRepos EITHER, which clause 4 does not already say: that clause governs what is CLONED, and so is silent about a directory that was never a clone. The gap was occupied until 2026-08-31 by GitRepos/.tools/rg, an unpacked ripgrep 14.1.0 that GitHub Copilot Chat downloaded on 2026-05-21, in a session on MAM-basics.code-workspace, after `winget install --id BurntSushi.ripgrep` returned 'No package found matching input criteria' -- the real ids are BurntSushi.ripgrep.MSVC and BurntSushi.ripgrep.GNU -- and `choco` turned out not to be installed. It never reached any PATH: Copilot referenced it by absolute path from its own generated one-liners, so nothing inherited it, and nothing missed it once Copilot stopped being used. Ben's decision, 2026-08-31: removed, 12.4 MB in 15 files, and no managed ripgrep installed in its place, there being no consumer to serve -- Codex CLI ships two copies of its own rg.exe and Claude Code vendors one per platform, so the agents that search this tree already carry the tool. THE ONE PERMITTED NON-REPO RESIDENT IS A SIBLING WORKTREE, GitRepos/<repo>-<topic>, which py/repo_util/git_worktree_cleanup.py's module docstring describes as deliberate practice. That exception states the test rather than opening a list: a worktree is git-managed and self-explaining, answering both `git worktree list` and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, where a loose directory answers neither and so becomes a puzzle for whoever next compares GitRepos against this roster. The scope check recorded in doc/PLAN-repo-maintenance-across-GitRepos.md makes exactly that comparison with Get-ChildItem -Directory, and .tools surfaced there as present-but-unlisted, indistinguishable from real drift -- surfacing with or without -Force, since a plain mkdir of a dot-name on Windows sets no hidden attribute. Barring such directories outright was chosen over declaring the permitted ones, for the reason clause 4 gives: a register of permitted extras would be a second roster to keep in sync with the first.

gists.comment: A gist's clone URL cannot be derived from its name and `gh repo list` cannot see a gist at all, so a gist not recorded somewhere is unrecoverable. BOTH OF BEN'S GISTS ARE HERE, and both entries are the only record on this machine that their gist exists. Neither is in any workspace file, so under clause 1 neither is cloned on a fresh machine, and as of 2026-08-31 neither is cloned on this machine either. Each went the same way, Gist-Hebrew-World first and Gist-ArtScroll a few hours later, on Ben's decision each time: the gist's content was evacuated into MAM-basics as py/author_misc/review_of_hebrew_worlds_phonetic_bible.py and py/author_misc/review_of_artscroll_transliterated_linear_siddur.py respectively, both rendered to MAM-with-doc/gh-pages/misc/, the gist itself was cut down to a stub pointing at its rendered page, and the clone was removed. BOTH GISTS NOW HOLD EXACTLY THEIR STUB AND NOTHING ELSE, which is newer than those evacuations and worth saying because the two did not always match: Gist-ArtScroll also carried a .gitattributes forcing LF, added by its 44831f8 on 2026-08-07 'matching the other repos', where Gist-Hebrew-World was never given one at all. That .gitattributes was removed on 2026-08-31 by Gist-ArtScroll's 95c8039 (Ben's decision) as spent -- a stub nobody expects to edit again gets nothing from a rule about how a future edit would be stored -- and the removal rewrote nothing, git ls-files --eol reporting the stub LF in the index and in the working tree either way. Nothing in this repo enforced that rule on either gist in the first place: check_repo_standards.py's GITATTRIBUTES_LF iterates workspace folders and neither gist is one, so no report changed. Do not treat the absence of a clone as a reason to drop an entry: the absence is what makes these load-bearing. THIS KEY HELD ONLY GIST-HEBREW-WORLD UNTIL 2026-08-31, and the reason is worth recording, because it stops the arrangement being re-proposed. Gist-ArtScroll was then in the roster, so its URL belonged in py/repo_util/repo_selection.py's _NON_REPO_WORKSPACE_FOLDERS, which clause 3 names as the implementation of record, and one URL in two files is one too many; this key held exactly the gist that map omitted. De-listing Gist-ArtScroll ended that split -- the map classifies WORKSPACE FOLDERS and there is no longer a workspace folder to classify -- so the URL moved here rather than being lost with the entry. The two homes are still not interchangeable: a gist that ever rejoins a workspace file wants its URL in that map, not here.

repos_to_keep_absent.comment: DOCUMENTATION, NOT A MECHANISM -- read gitrepos_setup_rule first, which is what actually decides. Under that rule's clause 4 the roster is an inclusion list, so a repo absent from all-repos.code-workspace is never cloned whether or not it appears here, and nothing consults this key at clone time. It exists only to record WHY a particular absence was chosen, in the one case where the reason is worth keeping. Most absent repos therefore get no entry at all and should not be given one: omission needs no justification, and a register that tried to name every repo Ben does not want would be a second roster to keep in sync with the first. This key held the whole exclusion mechanism for a few hours on 2026-08-31, between the first version of gitrepos_setup_rule -- which enumerated GitHub and subtracted -- and Ben's rejection of that version the same day as too broad. It is NOT frozen_repos, and neither may be derived from the other, exactly as the comment at the top of this file says of frozen_repos and in/vendoring_policy.json: a frozen repo's clone is kept, merely left untouched so its last-changed date keeps testifying to the pause.

al-hatorah.local_only_material: One stash, 892a7c82 'On main: wip: cb-qamats simplification uncertain keep' of 2026-04-23, existed on no remote. It was saved to C:/tmp/al-hatorah-stash-892a7c82.patch on 2026-08-31, reviewed the same day, and DISCARDED that day on Ben's decision; the patch file was deleted, so there is nothing left to apply. IT WAS SUPERSEDED, which reverses this clause's earlier claim that it was not. The stash was pure plumbing: +63/-44 on py/aht_phon/apply_aht_distinctions_to_mam.py over base commit 40fe97b4, converting four ad-hoc dtx dict keys (dtx-in-cb-qamats-arg, dtx-cb-qamats-peer-seq-mam, dtx-cb-qamats-peer-el-mam, dtx-cb-qamats-disputed-prev-cluster-idxs) into explicit keyword arguments. It changed no behavior: the inference itself, _sheva_override_for_qamats_following_sheva and _disputed_qamats_prev_cluster_indexes, is not in the diff at all. The commit IMMEDIATELY AFTER that base, 6978f8e4 of 2026-04-24 'Refactor qamats handling: move 4 frozen cases into overrides', deleted the entire mechanism -- -116/+8 on that one file -- and replaced it with four one-line data files: in/overrides/Mikhah/2.txt, in/overrides/Shemuel I/13.txt, in/overrides/Yeshayahu/48.txt and in/overrides/Yeshayahu/60.txt. So Ben stashed a simplification of the mechanism's internals at 22:52 and replaced the whole mechanism with data the next day. All four override files are still present in MAM-private/al-hatorah, among 26. The replacement works: 6978f8e4 also removed 34 lines from out/a01-phonetic-merges.json, and that merge log now holds no Micah section at all, its only Isaiah and 1Samuel entries being I10:17 and 1S12:24, so the four disputed-qamats chapters are clean. Nothing named force_sheva_na, peer_seq_mam, peer_el_mam, disputed_prev or sheva_override survives anywhere under al-hatorah/py/, and `git apply --check` skipped the sole hunk against the live 205-line file. THREE FIGURES IN THE ORIGINAL SAVE NOTE WERE WRONG and are corrected here: the base is 273 lines, not 315 (git hash-object on the blob fetched at ref 40fe97b4 returns 3734afc5..., matching the patch's own index line), the stash's version was 292 lines, not 334, and cb-qamats is NOT absent from the live code -- it appears in nine modules under al-hatorah/py/, so the construct is fully handled and only the merge-step special-casing went away. The claim that the stash was not superseded rested on counting added lines that are absent from the live file, which measures a refactor whose subject had been deleted and so cannot tell superseded from unfinished. WHEN A STASH LOOKS UNSUPERSEDED, READ THE COMMITS THAT FOLLOW ITS BASE, not just the live file.
al-hatorah.not_local_only: The branch feat/override-diff-viewer read 'ahead 6, behind 2' and looked like unpushed work. It was not: those six commits are ancestors of the live refs/heads/main, and the branch no longer exists on origin, so the remote-tracking ref it was measured against was stale. TEST AGAINST `git ls-remote`, NOT AGAINST refs/remotes/ -- a stale remote-tracking ref makes `git log --not --remotes` report local-only work as safely pushed, and would have done so here.
